name: Subscriptions, utilities and recurring bills
one_line: The standing-service-account situation on the Finance schema: utility statements, telecom bills, paid-subscription renewals, plan changes, cancellations and usage records. It requires evidence of an ongoing paid relationship, recommends institution then record_type, and sends isolated transaction records to a residual instead of manufacturing a subscription group.
design_cite: 00 names the field vocabulary outright: “Finance files may use institution, account type, tax year, and record type.” It names the broader situations this row extends as “financial records, travel, legal matters, creative projects, software repositories, personal administration, and photo collections” and states what templates eventually carry: “Each template should define the domain’s allowed fact fields, detection signals, recommended folder dimensions, preferred dimension order, optional branch patterns, privacy rules, and validation constraints.” 00 does not name subscriptions, utilities or recurring bills as their own situation, so every domain-specific claim below is inference rather than design.

proposed_fields.why_no_existing_key_works: A recurring record commonly labels the interval it covers, and that interval is the anchor that separates a service statement from a one-off receipt and one cycle from the next. creation_date is the filesystem or document timestamp of this file version, not the covered interval. tax_year is explicitly the tax year a Finance record belongs to, not a monthly bill cycle. term and application_cycle are scoped to other schemas. The broader name record_period is proposed instead of a private billing_period key because the same gap appears in account statements, coverage periods and other record series. This is an R1c proposal only; until adopted, period text remains evidence and never a legal fact.
proposed_fields.note: Direct only from an explicit labelled start/end range or period slot. A date in a filename, a statement date, a due date or a renewal date does not fill it. It is search and grouping support, never a folder level: per-cycle branches would fragment the service history into tiny folders.

deterministic: a utility-statement structure on one document: an issuing provider at a word boundary in a title, letterhead or labelled issuer slot, a labelled service or account identifier, a labelled billing or service period, and a labelled amount-due, usage or charge-summary block. The labels and their locations are the evidence; an amount and provider name by themselves are not. 00 supplies the source rule: “Deterministic extractors create direct facts when the information comes from a reliable, explicit source, such as a content hash, EXIF timestamp, a document title, or a labeled form field.”

a recurring-subscription lifecycle structure: an issuing provider together with a labelled plan, product, membership or subscription slot and an explicit recurring-cycle, next-renewal, paid-through, auto-renewal, cancellation or service-end slot. The lifecycle slot is what separates this situation from a one-time order made from the same seller; the context terms are proposals, not words attributed to 00.

a telecom or bundled-service bill whose account summary separates current recurring service charges from one-time activity and labels the covered period. A plan name may support account_type only when it appears in a labelled service or product slot; marketing copy elsewhere on the page stays an observation.

an email record whose labelled sender resolves to the provider, whose labelled subject carries a bill, renewal, plan-change, payment or cancellation term, and whose body supplies a labelled account, service, plan, period or next-billing slot. 00 says the email extractor yields “sender, recipients, subject, sent date, thread identifiers, message body, attachment names, and reply-chain context, while treating addresses and message content as potentially sensitive”; source_type email never fires alone.

a provider usage export whose sheet names or header cells label a service/account identifier, covered interval, usage unit and usage values. 00 says spreadsheet extraction yields “sheet names, column headers, visible cell values, table-like regions, formulas only when useful, and dates or identifiers from labeled cells.” A bare time series without the service/account labels remains a sparse group candidate rather than a domain fact writer.

an archive whose manifest shows a repeating family of service-statement, renewal-receipt or usage-export members. 00 requires: “Archives should be inspected without being unpacked to disk.” The member paths are observations; the outer archive name and download session prove neither institution nor account_type.

a final-bill or cancellation record whose labelled provider and service/account slot co-occur with an explicit final service period, paid-through date, service-end state or cancellation state. A generic cancellation email with no paid service or account evidence remains unresolved.
needs_llm: a service email that reads like a renewal or price-change notice but is formatted like marketing mail; the model must decide whether it records an existing paid relationship or merely solicits one, from a bounded dossier with citations

a utility or telecom bill with an unusual, multilingual or unlabelled layout where the provider, service period and account relationship are legible only from prose. 00 names “multilingual documents”, “indirect language” and “unlabeled forms” among the cases fixed patterns cannot safely cover

an OCR'd screenshot from a provider app: deciding whether it is an account bill, a subscription-management screen, a one-time checkout receipt, a product comparison or a generic capture. 00 names the same visual ambiguity: a PNG “may be a screenshot of a receipt, application portal, conversation, code error, or research figure”

whether bills, usage exports, renewal messages and cancellation confirmations form one coherent service-account lifecycle. This is a P9 group-coherence judgement; no sparse member receives institution, account_type or record_period from its neighbours

a signed service document that mixes plan pricing with party recitals, obligations and an execution block; the bounded question is whether Finance and Legal are both plausible, not which permanent path wins

whether a notice from a membership organization is an ordinary paid subscription, an insurance policy, an HOA assessment or evidence of a professional credential. Shared recurrence language is not enough to pick among the roster templates
never_alone: a provider or organization name alone. Providers also send marketing, privacy policies, outage notices and product announcements. Word boundaries remain required by 00: “It should use word-boundary matching rather than substring matching.”

the words subscription, plan, membership, renewal, recurring, bill or statement alone. A research plan, floor plan, insurance renewal, credential renewal, bank statement and newsletter subscription all use the same vocabulary
a currency amount, due date, renewal date or date range alone. A one-time receipt, quotation, insurance notice, lease and event reminder can each carry one; a bare 4-digit token is never tax_year

a masked digit string alone. It may be an account number, subscription identifier, order number, policy number, case number, device serial or tracking number; only a labelled slot plus situation context gives it a role

source_type or extension alone, including PDF, email, spreadsheet, image, archive, opaque binary or calendar. 00 says to “treat the file extension as a routing signal rather than an assumption about meaning”
a recurring calendar event or reminder. Calendar is a SOURCE_TYPE, and an event titled Cancel trial or Pay internet bill is the user's reminder rather than a record issued by the provider

a recurring merchant line inside a bank or card statement. The merchant is content of finance.personal-records, not the issuer of this situation; copying it into institution would invert the field's role

a service address alone. The same address appears on a lease, insurance declarations, delivery receipt, property record and utility bill, and the Finance schema does not declare a service-address field
membership in a download session with several bills. 00 is explicit: “A session should never be treated as proof of topic”; it is a retrieval clue and review aid only
the absence of EXIF on a bill capture read as screenshot proof. 00 says “the system must not mistake the absence of EXIF for proof that an image is a screenshot”
a provider-shaped filename on an encrypted or unreadable PDF. 00 says the system “should not infer a purpose from their filename alone” for unreadable, encrypted, corrupted or unsupported material

grouping_reasons: one standing service account across its statements, usage exports, payment confirmations, plan changes and final bill. A repeated labelled account or subscription identifier is the anchor evidence; until a canonical identifier field exists, it stays evidence rather than a fact
one paid subscription across sign-up, renewal receipts, plan changes and cancellation. The lifecycle is a P9 group, not a new status field or one folder per renewal cycle
one utility service across a statement and its provider-generated usage export. A sparse export may join the group without copying institution or record_period from the statement
one bill-payment family: bill, autopay notice and payment confirmation for the same labelled account and covered period. A shared amount alone is not the join
one provider bundle only when a single labelled account actually covers several services. A provider name alone must not merge unrelated mobile, home-internet and media subscriptions
one duplicate or corrected statement family through the universal duplicate_family and version_family facts, never by interpreting a duplicate-looking suffix as proof

template.why: institution leads because a leaf such as Bill, Renewal, Usage or Cancellation is unintelligible until the issuing provider is known. This applies 00's parent-context rule: “A work type such as Homework 3 is meaningful only after the course is known, and a course code may require the school or term to disambiguate it.” record_type is the leaf that separates the lifecycle documents. account_type remains legal but is omitted from the default: a bundled statement may cover several services, while a one-service provider would create a meaningless one-child level. Where a labelled service or plan value materially separates several accounts under one institution, the user may insert account_type between the two. tax_year is not a level because a monthly service period or renewal date is not a tax year. Proposed record_period is search/grouping metadata only; a folder per billing cycle would fragment one service history, and 00 requires the canvas to warn when a level “creates a large number of tiny folders” and to “recommend flattening when a dimension does not materially improve retrieval.” The recommendation is shallow and editable: “The system recommends an order based on the domain template, but the user can reverse, remove, add, or flatten dimensions.” It is not time-first: “For document and record domains, project, function, or subject usually comes before time because putting year first scatters related work across calendar folders.”

collides_with.signal: A utility or subscription bill and a bank or card statement each carry an institution, a labelled period and a balance or amount. The discriminating evidence is structural: a labelled service address, service/account identifier, meter/usage table or subscription lifecycle slot belongs here; a financial-account descriptor plus a beginning/ending balance reported by the institution that holds the account belongs to finance.personal-records. A merchant line inside that statement never becomes this row's institution.

The shared evidence item is a named seller plus a charge or confirmation. A labelled service period, standing account/subscription identifier, plan and next-billing or cancellation state makes it recurring-account material; a single order or transaction identifier, item rows and a labelled total with no standing relationship makes it a one-off receipt. A renewal receipt can support both readings; when the recurrence structure is absent, abstention from this template is correct.

A service agreement and a recurring bill share the provider, service address, plan and recurring fee. The discriminating evidence is what the document does: party recitals, obligations and an execution block create an agreement; a service/account identifier plus a covered period, usage or billed amount reports on the running account. A signed agreement may activate Finance and Legal on disjoint evidence; one shared provider name or fee must not count twice.

An HOA dues or assessment notice and a utility bill both repeat, name an organization, carry a property address and request payment. Association governance, unit or lot references, assessments, covenants or meeting context point to the HOA situation; a metered service, usage unit, rate plan, service identifier or paid subscription plan points here. The address and recurring amount alone decide neither.

A home utility bill and a property record can share a service address, account reference and amount. A recurring service period, meter or usage table and next-billing structure points here; title, ownership, inspection, improvement, permit or warranty structure points to the household-property situation. A service address alone activates neither.

A premium invoice or policy-renewal notice and a paid-subscription renewal each name a provider, period and recurring charge. A labelled policy number, named insured, coverage line, limit or deductible belongs to insurance; a service plan, access period, usage unit or subscription lifecycle state belongs here. Renewal vocabulary and an amount are shared evidence and cannot choose the template.

falls_through_to.why: 00 defines this residual for “isolated invoices, delivery confirmations, booking records, boarding passes, purchase receipts, event tickets, and similar transactional documents.” A renewal receipt, autopay confirmation or final payment that lacks an accepted service-account group is exactly that broad transactional record.

00 defines it for “standalone certificates, notices, confirmations, forms, and PDFs that have a durable purpose but no broader group.” A cancellation confirmation, service-closure notice or terms-change notice with no accepted lifecycle group fits that definition.

00 includes “account statements” among this residual's sensitive isolated material. Utility and telecom statements can expose a service address, account identifier, household name and usage history, so a safety-only file with no deeper accepted group is offered this protected home.

00 defines it for “screenshots that appear time-sensitive or remind the user of something but have no accepted project, trip, application, or event relationship.” A provider-app amount-due capture with no accepted account group belongs in that controlled review path, not in a fabricated provider folder.

00 defines it for “files whose meaning is partly understood but whose final location requires a future decision.” A sparse usage export or calendar reminder whose standing account cannot be identified is that case.

00 defines it for “password-protected archives, unreadable documents, damaged files, and unknown formats” and permits the safer option of representing them without moving. An encrypted bill is not rescued by its provider-shaped filename.

sensitivity_why: This is a Finance-schema template and inherits the safety posture 00 names: “Finance, identity, medical, and legal material should be implemented first as safety domains, meaning the system detects and protects them before any cloud or automated placement decision is allowed.” Utility and telecom statements are account records, for which 00 says: “A scanned passport, tax statement, medical document, authentication key, or account record should enter a protected state immediately.” The visible branch stays redacted and local-first: “a Finance or Identity proposal may be visible as a protected area, but the product should avoid showing sensitive filenames or sending their contents to cloud services by default.” Only the catalogue value potentially_sensitive is set here; D2's authoritative ClassificationRecord and P7's handling-class decision are not re-derived or assigned by this row.
open_question: Should R1c adopt record_period as one shared, destination-ineligible canonical field for labelled billing, statement, coverage and other record intervals, or should those intervals remain raw evidence only? This row proposes the broad key because creation_date and tax_year are demonstrably different roles, but it does not place the key in dimension_order and works without it. If Joseph rejects the field, the recurring interval remains a deterministic activation signal and P9 grouping anchor rather than a file fact.
